Because I do not download data, the pixel-level NDWI/NDVI change map must be run by a person. Here is the exact script:

```python
import earthaccess, xarray as xr, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

earthaccess.login()

# --- Granule IDs ---
pre_id  = "MOD09GA.A2024294.h18v05.061.2024298001757"
post_id = "MOD09GA.A2024304.h18v05.061.2024306200636"

# Download both tiles (h18v05 covers Valencia city + coastal plain)
results_pre  = earthaccess.search_data(short_name="MOD09GA", granule_ur=pre_id)
results_post = earthaccess.search_data(short_name="MOD09GA", granule_ur=post_id)
files_pre  = earthaccess.download(results_pre,  "./pre")
files_post = earthaccess.download(results_post, "./post")

# Open with xarray (pyhdf or rioxarray for HDF-EOS2)
import rioxarray as rxr
pre  = rxr.open_rasterio(files_pre[0],  masked=True)
post = rxr.open_rasterio(files_post[0], masked=True)

# NDWI = (Green - NIR) / (Green + NIR)  [Band 4 = Green, Band 2 = NIR in MOD09GA]
# Bands are 1-indexed in the SDS; adjust for 0-indexed array slicing
green_pre  = pre.sel(band=4)  / 10000.0
nir_pre    = pre.sel(band=2)  / 10000.0
green_post = post.sel(band=4) / 10000.0
nir_post   = post.sel(band=2) / 10000.0

ndwi_pre  = (green_pre  - nir_pre)  / (green_pre  + nir_pre)
ndwi_post = (green_post - nir_post) / (green_post + nir_post)

# Flood mask: pixels where NDWI flipped from <0.0 to >0.3
flood_mask = (ndwi_pre < 0.0) & (ndwi_post > 0.3)

# Clip to Valencia bounding box
bbox = dict(x=slice(-0.8, 0.2), y=slice(40.0, 38.8))
flood_clip = flood_mask.rio.clip_box(**bbox)

# Area estimate: each 500m pixel = 0.25 km²
n_flooded = int(flood_clip.sum())
area_km2  = n_flooded * 0.25
print(f"Estimated inundated area: {area_km2:.1f} km²  ({n_flooded} pixels @ 500 m)")

# Plot
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
ndwi_pre.rio.clip_box(**bbox).plot(ax=axes[0], vmin=-0.5, vmax=0.5, cmap="RdBu", title="NDWI Pre (20 Oct)")
ndwi_post.rio.clip_box(**bbox).plot(ax=axes[1], vmin=-0.5, vmax=0.5, cmap="RdBu", title="NDWI Post (30 Oct)")
flood_clip.plot(ax=axes[2], cmap="Blues", title=f"Flood extent (~{area_km2:.0f} km²)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("valencia_flood_extent.png", dpi=150)
```
